title: Predictive rollback signatures and tier-aware routing for heterogeneous canary rollouts
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: As customers run heterogeneous canary deployments (mix of quantized/FP16 variants, different token-length profiles, and multi-region pools), we need an automated, signal-driven rollback mechanism that is aware of routing tiers and regional failover. Current rollback rules are simple threshold-based (error-rate or latency p95) and do not distinguish signal skew introduced by traffic tiering, capacity degradation, or region-specific degradation. This ticket implements: 1) a compact, predictive \"rollback signature\" (a short vector of normalized signals) that captures multi-dimensional degradation across regions and tiers; 2) a tier-aware routing adapter that weights canary traffic by proximity and capacity while preserving signal fidelity; and 3) an automated rollback decision engine with simulated safety checks and manual override hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Define rollback signature schema that fits in 256 bytes when serialized to JSON (for tracing and storage)
Implement service that computes rollback signatures per canary segment (region x tier x model-variant) every minute
Routing adapter applies proximity-weight and capacity-weighted sampling while annotating requests so signatures are interpretable
Rollback engine evaluates signatures against baseline using both absolute thresholds and trend-delta checks, supports auto-rollback and canary pause, and emits audit logs and rollback rationale

Automated simulation harness that runs 100 synthetic failure scenarios (region outage, kernel OOM, quantization regressions, degraded KV cache) and shows expected rollback decisions >= 95% match with manual policy table
End-to-end tests and a runbook for on-call with clear escalation steps and view in Console rollout timeline

updates: 2026-02-19: Kickoff meeting notes added to Confluence (link below). Agreed on two-phase delivery: phase 1 (signature + offline simulation), phase 2 (routing adapter + auto-rollback).
2026-02-25: Initial signature draft: [latency_p50, latency_p95, error_rate, token_throughput, kv_cache_miss_rate, kernel_oom_rate, tail_lock_contention]. Normalization to z-score per-region proposed.

2026-03-02: Prototype rollback engine (offline) produced on staging trace data. Early results show detection of quantization regressions with 89% recall and 2.3% false-positive rate on historical incidents.

2026-03-08: Routing adapter prototype completed. Uses capacity-weighted sampling and adds 'sampling_bucket' and 'proximity_weight' annotations to requests. Initial perf impact < 0.5% latency increase under load tests.
2026-03-11: Simulation harness ran 100 scenarios. 94 scenarios produced rollback decisions matching expected table; investigating 6 mismatches (mostly subtle KV-cache warmup behavior).
2026-03-12: Rolling this ticket into in-progress; Diego pairing with SRE to tune hysteresis windows and add manual override in Console before enabling auto-rollback in staging.

Diego Alvarez (2026-03-02): Offline prototype uses rolling 5-min windows with 30s slide. Need to evaluate longer windows for low-traffic regions to reduce noise.
Riley Park - SRE (2026-03-08): Confirmed that adding annotations does not break existing tracing backends. We should emit signature version and seed for reproducibility.
QA Lead - Priya Nair (2026-03-11): Tests failing in one scenario where regional throttles produced transient spikes. Add test case for 'tiered throttling during failover' to the harness.
metrics: Primary: reduce mean time to detect/regress (MTTD) for canary regressions from 12m to <=4m
Safety: false positive rate for auto-rollback <= 5% on historical incidents
Operational: end-to-end added latency from routing adapter < 1% p95
Coverage: simulation harness covers >= 95% of defined failure templates
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: noisy signals in low-traffic regions may trigger spurious rollback. Mitigation: adaptive windowing and fallback to canary pause instead of full rollback.
Risk: tight coupling between routing adapter and tracing could cause instrumentation regressions. Mitigation: versioned annotations and backward-compatible tracing consumers.
Risk: customers on Dedicated may see traffic reshaping during tests. Mitigation: limit initial rollout to internal tenants and opt-in enterprise customers.
